title: Anomalous Weak Pointer Shifts as Postselected Interference among Coarse-Grained Histories
abstract: Anomalous weak values and superoscillations allow a pointer to exhibit an effective shift outside the eigenvalue range of the measured observable. We reformulate this effect in a phase-space path-integral language. For each eigenvalue branch $a_j$ of the measured observable, {the interaction couples $a_j$ to the pointer position $\hat{x}_p$ and thereby translates the conjugate pointer momentum by $γa_j$.} After postselection, {the branch-conditioned amplitudes are coherently superposed with coefficients chosen to produce a superoscillatory approximation. When this conditional amplitude acts on an initial pointer momentum wavepacket for which the finite superoscillatory-window condition is satisfied, the resulting momentum wavefunction behaves as if it had been translated by $γA_w$, rather than by any of the eigenvalue-conditioned shifts $γa_j$. This yields an effective path-integral representation of anomalous weak pointer shifts and motivates their interpretation in terms of interference among finite coarse-grained histories.} We discuss how this picture bears on conservation-law questions.
summary: This paper develops a phase-space path-integral formalism to explain anomalous weak pointer shifts. It shows that these seemingly unusual shifts are mathematically equivalent to constructive interference among multiple coarse-grained quantum histories. This offers a powerful, intuitive picture of measurement outcomes while maintaining consistency with fundamental conservation laws in the full closed system.
main_problem: The paper reformulates anomalous weak pointer shifts, which allow effective measurements outside an observable's eigenvalue range, by interpreting them as interference among coarse-grained histories.
main_result: The postselected momentum distribution behaves as if it were translated by an effective shift $\gamma A_w$, providing a path-integral representation of the anomalous weak value effect via history interference.
method: The analysis uses phase-space path integrals, applying superoscillatory approximations to sum over branch-conditioned amplitudes derived from measurement coupling.
model_or_system: The model involves a quantum system ($\hat{A}_s$) coupled weakly to a pointer observable ($\hat{x}_p$), analyzed using path integral techniques and focusing on the resulting momentum readout.

important_parameters: The coupling constant ($\gamma$) and the window size defining the superoscillatory approximation.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on satisfying a finite superoscillatory-window condition for the initial momentum wavepacket, and it is explicitly noted not to be a complete resolution of all conservation law puzzles.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by introducing the anomalous shift, reformulating it in path integrals using branch conditioning, applying superoscillatory approximations to derive an effective momentum translation, and finally analyzing how this structure relates to symmetry constraints via Ward identities.
why_interesting: It provides a deep theoretical interpretation of weak measurements and pointer shifts within the framework of quantum histories, connecting non-classical measurement outcomes to fundamental concepts like interference and conservation laws in a path-integral setting.
